chosen_concept.prompt: One straight modular section of a wooden plank pier: a flat rectangular deck of weathered driftwood planks running crosswise, on four thick round driftwood piles at the corners that extend well below the deck, diagonal X cross-bracing between the piles, barnacles and a little green-teal seaweed on the lower parts of the piles. Both short ends are cut clean and flat so the section tiles seamlessly lengthwise. No railings, no water shown, isolated module. Real size about 2.4 m wide x 3.6 m long; deck 0.55 m above water, piles extend 2.5 m below the deck. Stylised Palworld/Animo-class game prop concept, one coherent family with Quaternius-style medieval/fantasy wood and stone assets: chunky readable shapes, warm weathered driftwood timber, sun-bleached rope, teal and sea-blue paint accents, cream sailcloth, clean hand-painted PBR finish. Use the attached boards only for palette, mood, maritime timber/stone/blue language and finish quality. Absolutely no red, no oxblood, no crimson anywhere. Single isolated object, full object visible, plain neutral light background, no text, no labels, no people, no creatures. IMPORTANT proportions: the deck is a long narrow rectangle, 1.5 times longer than wide (2.4 m wide by 3.6 m long), planks running across the short width. The piles are tall: they extend about 2.5 m below the deck underside, so the total height (top of deck to pile foot) is about 3 m, close to the deck length. Six piles: three along each long side. Deck surface is flat with no posts sticking up above it.

rejected_concepts.reason: reads as a square stool: deck not 2.4x3.6 rectangular and piles too short for 2.5 m below-deck depth
